clips.title: STOP Using Tsc and Node To Run TypeScript Use THIS instead - Supercharge Your Workflow
clips.why: A short, friendly tour of tsx, the tool that runs a .ts file directly, which is what the platform uses while you work and in every test.
look: How tsx is used: one command in front of a .ts file, with no build step in between.
Keep the lesson's warning in mind while you watch: tsx is fast because it removes types without checking them.
clips.after: In the platform, tsx runs every test and every dev command, and tsc stays the gate that actually checks the types.

clips.title: How to Setup Node.js with TypeScript in 2023
clips.why: In under three minutes this shows the same steps as the lab: TypeScript added to a Node project, a tsconfig, and the changes that ES modules need.
look: The tsconfig.json part: which options make TypeScript follow Node's rules.
The ES modules part at the end: "type": "module" in package.json and what changes for imports.
clips.after: The platform makes these choices once, in tsconfig.base.json with NodeNext, and every service package shares them.

clips.title: '.js' files in TypeScript - why?!
clips.why: Matt Pocock explains in under three minutes the rule that crashed the image in the story: why a TypeScript import must end in .js.
look: The problem he starts from: TypeScript refuses an import that has no .js, like the TS2835 error you will see in the lab.
Why Node wants .js: Node loads the file that exists after the build.
Why not .ts: the source file is not what runs.
clips.after: This is the one rule tsx forgives and Node does not, so in our repo tsc with NodeNext catches it before any image is built.

clips.title: Npm workspaces tutorial
clips.why: Shows how one package in a workspace uses code from another by name, which is how every platform service uses the shared package.
look: Handling internal dependencies: a workspace package listed as a dependency of another.
Referencing code from the other package by its name, with no relative path.
clips.after: In the platform, gateway, broker, orchestrator, harness and Slack app all import the shared package this way, with one lockfile for all of them.

practice.q: You run npx tsx src/main.ts and it prints nova/undefined with no error. Which command would have caught the bug before anyone ran it?

options.why: tsx has no type checking to switch on. However you call it, it only removes types and runs the code.
tsc reads every file and reports TS2339: the property does not exist. --noEmit means it only checks and writes nothing.
Node's own type stripping removes types just like tsx does, and checks nothing.

practice.q: src/branch.ts sits next to src/main.ts. Complete the import so it works with tsx, passes tsc with NodeNext, and still works after the build.
practice.hint: Name the file Node will load after the build, not the file in your editor.
practice.why: After the build only dist/branch.js exists, and Node loads exactly the path you wrote. tsx maps ./branch.js back to branch.ts while you develop.

practice.q: A teammate's import ./branch works in dev, and typecheck is clean, yet the image crashes with ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND. What did they most likely change in tsconfig.json?

options.why: strict is about types such as null and any. It has nothing to do with how imports are resolved.
bundler resolution allows imports without an ending, the way Vite does. But Node, not a bundler, loads the built files, so the missing .js only shows up in the image.
That would give errors about process and node:fs, not accept a missing ending.

practice.q: Make npm write exact versions such as 5.9.3 instead of ^5.9.3 for every future install. What goes into .npmrc?
practice.hint: Two words joined by a hyphen: save and how precise.
practice.why: save-exact=true makes npm drop the ^, so a version only changes when someone changes it in a pull request.

practice.q: Put the life of a change in order, from your laptop to a running container.
items: You run the code with tsx while you work on it
CI runs npm run typecheck (tsc --noEmit) on the pull request
The build runs tsc and writes dist/main.js
The image starts node dist/main.js, with no TypeScript tools inside
practice.why: tsx gives a fast loop, tsc is the gate before merge, and the built JavaScript is what really runs.
